Thought: Let me analyze this reaction. 4-Bromobenzoyl is an acyl halide (specifically a benzoyl chloride derivative where bromine is at the 4-position of the benzene ring). Pentanoic acid is a carboxylic acid. When an acyl halide reacts with a carboxylic acid, they typically form a carboxylic acid anhydride. This is a nucleophilic acyl substitution reaction where the carboxylate group from the pentanoic acid attacks the carbonyl carbon of the acyl halide, displacing the halide.

The reaction would produce a mixed anhydride between 4-bromobenzoic acid and pentanoic acid, which is a carboxylic acid anhydride.
